_doc: Plain-language clinical significance of an out-of-range result, keyed by lab_catalog.json analyte key. Used by clinical_insights.py.
high / low / reactive: what a result in that direction can indicate. General reference knowledge only; wording says 'can' / 'may' because one value never establishes a diagnosis.

concern: the directions that are clinically adverse. A result outside the range in any other direction (e.g. a high HDL on a report that prints '<40' as its range) is not reported as abnormal. Omitted = both directions.

hba1c.high: Reflects average blood glucose over about 3 months; a raised value indicates hyperglycaemia over that period (above the diabetes control target when diabetes is recorded).

haemoglobin.high: Can reflect dehydration, smoking, lung disease or a raised red cell mass.
haemoglobin.low: Indicates anaemia; lower values reduce oxygen delivery and can cause fatigue, breathlessness and palpitations.

glucose_fasting.high: Fasting hyperglycaemia; in the diabetic range it reflects inadequate glucose control.
glucose_fasting.low: Hypoglycaemia; risk is higher with insulin or sulfonylureas.

glucose_pp.high: Post-meal hyperglycaemia; reflects how well glucose is handled after food.
glucose_pp.low: Hypoglycaemia; risk is higher with insulin or sulfonylureas.

glucose_random.high: Hyperglycaemia at the time of testing; interpret with fasting glucose or HbA1c.
glucose_random.low: Hypoglycaemia; risk is higher with insulin or sulfonylureas.

urea.high: Can reflect reduced kidney function, dehydration or high protein breakdown.
urea.low: Usually of little significance; can reflect low protein intake or liver disease.

bun.high: Can reflect reduced kidney function, dehydration or high protein breakdown.
bun.low: Usually of little significance; can reflect low protein intake or liver disease.

creatinine.high: Suggests reduced kidney filtration; relevant to the dosing and safety of kidney-cleared medicines.
creatinine.low: Usually reflects low muscle mass; rarely significant on its own.

egfr.low: Reduced kidney filtration; relevant to the dosing and safety of kidney-cleared medicines.

sodium.high: Hypernatraemia; usually reflects water loss or dehydration.
sodium.low: Hyponatraemia; can be caused by diuretics, some antidepressants or fluid imbalance, and can cause confusion or falls.

potassium.high: Hyperkalaemia; can affect heart rhythm. ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone and reduced kidney function raise it.
potassium.low: Hypokalaemia; can affect heart rhythm and muscles. Diuretics and diarrhoea or vomiting lower it.

chloride.high: Can accompany dehydration or acid-base disturbance.
chloride.low: Can accompany vomiting, diuretic use or acid-base disturbance.

calcium.high: Hypercalcaemia; can reflect parathyroid disease, excess vitamin D or calcium supplements, or malignancy.
calcium.low: Hypocalcaemia; often reflects low albumin or vitamin D, kidney disease or parathyroid problems; interpret with albumin.

phosphorus.low: Can reflect malnutrition, vitamin D deficiency or parathyroid disease.

uric_acid.high: Hyperuricaemia; raises the risk of gout and kidney stones and can be raised by diuretics.

albumin.low: Can reflect liver disease, kidney protein loss, malnutrition or inflammation; lowers measured total calcium.

total_protein.high: Can reflect dehydration or raised immunoglobulins.
total_protein.low: Can reflect liver disease, kidney protein loss or malnutrition.

bilirubin_total.high: Can reflect liver or bile-duct disease or increased red cell breakdown (haemolysis); can cause jaundice.

bilirubin_direct.high: Raised conjugated bilirubin points to liver or bile-duct (cholestatic) disease.

bilirubin_indirect.high: Raised unconjugated bilirubin can reflect red cell breakdown (haemolysis) or Gilbert syndrome.

ast.high: Liver cell injury (also released from muscle and heart); causes include fatty liver, alcohol, viral infection and some medicines.

alt.high: Liver cell injury; causes include fatty liver, alcohol, viral hepatitis and some medicines.

alp.high: Can reflect bile-duct (cholestatic) liver disease or bone disease.

ggt.high: Can reflect bile-duct disease, alcohol use or enzyme-inducing medicines.

tsh.high: Points to an underactive thyroid (or under-replacement when on levothyroxine).
tsh.low: Points to an overactive thyroid (or over-replacement when on levothyroxine).

t3.high: Can reflect an overactive thyroid or excess thyroid hormone.
t3.low: Can reflect an underactive thyroid or non-thyroidal illness.

t4.high: Can reflect an overactive thyroid or excess thyroid hormone.

ft3.high: Can reflect an overactive thyroid or excess thyroid hormone.
ft3.low: Can reflect an underactive thyroid or non-thyroidal illness.

ft4.high: Can reflect an overactive thyroid or excess thyroid hormone.

cholesterol.high: Raises long-term cardiovascular risk, especially with diabetes, hypertension or smoking.

ldl.high: The main atherogenic cholesterol; raises long-term cardiovascular risk.

hdl.low: Low protective cholesterol; adds to cardiovascular risk.

vldl.high: Tracks triglycerides; adds to cardiovascular risk.

triglycerides.high: Adds to cardiovascular risk; commonly raised with poor glucose control, obesity or alcohol. Very high levels raise pancreatitis risk.

wbc.high: Can reflect infection, inflammation, steroid use or stress.
wbc.low: Can reflect viral infection, medicine effects or bone-marrow problems; raises infection risk.

platelets.high: Can reflect inflammation, iron deficiency or a marrow disorder.
platelets.low: Raises bleeding risk; can follow viral infection (e.g. dengue), medicines or marrow problems.

rbc.high: Can reflect dehydration or a raised red cell mass.
rbc.low: Usually accompanies a low haemoglobin (anaemia); interpret with the haemoglobin result.

pcv.high: Can reflect dehydration or a raised red cell mass.
pcv.low: Usually accompanies a low haemoglobin (anaemia); interpret with the haemoglobin result.

mcv.high: Large red cells; can reflect vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol or some medicines (e.g. long-term metformin lowers B12).
mcv.low: Small red cells; commonly reflects iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait.

mch.high: Accompanies large red cells (B12 or folate deficiency).
mch.low: Pale red cells; commonly reflects iron deficiency.

mchc.high: Usually a measurement artefact or spherocytosis; rarely significant alone.
mchc.low: Pale red cells; commonly reflects iron deficiency.

rdw.high: Red cells of mixed sizes; often an early sign of iron, B12 or folate deficiency.

neutrophils.high: Commonly reflects bacterial infection, inflammation or steroid use.
neutrophils.low: Raises infection risk; can follow viral infection or medicines.

lymphocytes.low: Can follow acute illness, steroids or immune suppression.

monocytes.high: Can reflect chronic infection or inflammation.

eosinophils.high: Can reflect allergy, eczema or asthma, a drug reaction or parasitic infection.

basophils.high: Can accompany allergy or, rarely, a marrow disorder.

esr.high: Non-specific marker of inflammation or infection.

pt.high: Slower clotting; can reflect anticoagulant use, liver disease or vitamin K deficiency; raises bleeding risk.

inr.high: Slower clotting; can reflect anticoagulant effect or liver disease; raises bleeding risk.

vitamin_d.low: Vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency; affects bone health and calcium balance.

vitamin_b12.low: B12 deficiency; can cause anaemia and nerve symptoms such as tingling or numbness. Long-term metformin lowers B12.

ferritin.high: Can reflect inflammation, liver disease or iron overload.
ferritin.low: Depleted iron stores; the commonest cause of iron-deficiency anaemia.

iron.high: Can reflect iron overload or recent supplements.
iron.low: Can reflect iron deficiency or chronic inflammation.

crp.high: Marker of active inflammation or infection.

hiv.reactive: A reactive screening result needs confirmatory testing; HIV infection is not established by a screening test alone.

hbsag.reactive: Indicates current hepatitis B infection (acute or chronic); relevant to liver monitoring, liver-affecting medicines and household contacts.

hcv.reactive: Indicates hepatitis C exposure; active infection needs confirmation (HCV RNA).

vdrl.reactive: Screening test for syphilis; can be falsely positive and needs a confirmatory treponemal test.

urine_pregnancy.reactive: Positive pregnancy test; relevant to the safety of medicines and investigations.

dengue_ns1.reactive: Indicates early dengue infection; platelet count and warning signs are relevant.

dengue_igg.reactive: Indicates past or secondary dengue infection.

typhidot.reactive: Suggests recent typhoid infection; IgM tests can be falsely positive.
